R1 design point (Aug 2026): adopt Ga-doped p-type SHJ as the reference architecture at 60-90 um with a tracked path to 20-40 um; n-type is dropped - Cz n(P) shows no low-temperature annealing while p-type recovers, and 90 um Ga-SHJ recovered 97% after 1e14 e/cm2 cured at 80 C (CEA, ISFH-certified); the annealing cliff is processing- and fluence-dependent, not a pure thickness law; handling breakage at 60-100 um is a solved engineering problem on modern lines

R1 manufacturability (Aug 2026): the 10%-at-100um to 96%-at-70um breakage cliff traces to one 2016 CEA-INES pilot-line paper (Harrison et al., EU PVSEC) and is a state-of-the-line snapshot, since mitigated - CEA runs 60 um on the same line class (Cariou 2023), engineered handling achieved <5% breakage at 100 um (Terheiden 2015), edge reinforcement gives ~0% breakage at 28 um (Wu 2024), kerfless porous-Si layer transfer demonstrated 43 um at 19% (Petermann 2012), and Solestial flies ~20 um cells with polymer-film module support at 508 g/m2

R1 annealing cliff (Aug 2026): the cliff is not a fixed thickness wall - Solestial data (20 um full recovery / 80 um near-zero) was taken at 1e15 e/cm2 on Cz p(B), while CEA's 90 um 97% recovery was at 1e14 e/cm2 on Ga-doped SHJ; REDR theory predicts the annealing rate scales with the injection-to-defect ratio (which thinning raises), but no published quantitative thickness model exists and the hydrogen contribution from a-Si:H is explicitly unresolved

R1 system anchors (Aug 2026): III-V rigid panels run 100-150 W/kg at $200-400/W, III-V flexible 250-350 W/kg at $400-600/W; Solestial targets 500-600 W/kg and $20-40/W (company targets, marked post-2025) with a self-published 508 g/m2 module mass; NASA SBIR targets 200 W/kg array BOL and $40/W; no peer-reviewed measured module-level W/kg for coverglass-free thin Si exists, and no published ATOX ground-test data covers modern thin-Si polymer-encapsulated modules (heritage: LDEF dielectric-coating data)

evidence.locator: EU PVSEC 2016, 2BO.9.2 (via Wu et al. 2024 paraphrase)
evidence.paraphrase: CEA-INES SHJ pilot line: breakage rose from ~10% at 100 um to ~96% at 70 um in production mode on 156 mm wafers; handling/wet-processing/printing steps identified.
Edge-reinforced free-standing wafers: 28 um cell at 20.33% (certified 20.05%) with ~0% breakage vs >85% for all-thin 21-29 um controls; quotes the Harrison 2016 breakage figures.
Engineered handling on the Hanwha Q CELLS pilot line: <5% breakage for 100 um wafers through full cell processing, cells >20% efficient.
90 um and 60 um SHJ cells recovered 97% of initial performance after 1 MeV electrons at 1e14 e/cm2, cured at 80 C under representative conditions, certified by ISFH-Caltec.
CEA-INES manufactures 60 um Ga-doped SHJ on the pilot line (laser-cut in half after processing); 60 um beats 180 um PERC EOL at every fluence at 3x lower mass.
20 um SHJ: 120 mV/hr Voc recovery (electrons) and 7.5 mV/hr (protons), full recovery in 8 h at 80 C; 80 um nearly zero annealing; Cz p(B) ~90% vs Cz n(P) none at 100 C; 1-2 cells per condition.
Fermilab A2D2 irradiations of 20-80 um UT-Si to 1e15 e/cm2; isothermal annealing under light at 100 C showed major recovery; degradation did not follow NIEL scaling.
Bulk-hydrogenated Ga-PERC recovered full pre-irradiation lifetime after ~360 s at 380 C vs 71.5x longer unfired; fired samples recovered at 150 C where unfired did not.

CEA: bulk hydrogenation steps did not influence post-irradiation bulk lifetime prior to self-healing; Ga doping/resistivity strongly affects post-irradiation diffusion length (74 vs 354 um at 1.5e14 e/cm2 for 0.9 vs 20 ohm-cm).

60 um Ga-doped p-type alternative TOPCon on industry-representative equipment matched conventional p-PERC post-irradiation performance at ~3x lower mass; TOPCon less adapted to very thin wafers than SHJ.

Solestial comparison table: III-V rigid 100-150 W/kg at $200-400/W; III-V flexible 250-350 W/kg at $400-600/W; commodity-Si flexible 50-200 W/kg at $5-20/W; Solestial target 500-600 W/kg at $20-40/W (marked as post-2025 target specs).
Module mass 508 g/m2 including cells, interconnects, protective films; rollable to 5 cm bend radius; polymer/ceramic films replace coverglass.
SBIR Ignite targets: 200 W/kg BOL at array level, 50 kW/m3 stowed, $40/W manufacturing cost, >=10x cost reduction vs state of practice.
AO erodes unprotected Ag interconnects ~1.0 um per 1e20 atoms/cm2; SiO2/Al2O3/SiNx dielectric coatings protect; no quality polymer cover replacement demonstrated as of LDEF analysis.

operations.reason: Three sweeps converge: the handling cliff is a 2016 line snapshot now engineered around at 60-100 um and module-supported below; the annealing cliff moved between 2023 (near-zero at 80 um, 1e15 e/cm2, Cz p(B)) and 2025 (97% at 90 um, 1e14 e/cm2, Ga-SHJ, ISFH-certified), so the design point is set by doping and processing first and thickness second; the system anchors separate company targets from measured values. Perimeter: Harrison 2016 read via Wu 2024's paraphrase (paywalled); Guillot Solar RRL and Le 2026 full texts bot-walled; Solestial W/kg and $/W figures are company targets; the 40 um annealing point exists only graphically; no published ATOX ground test for thin-Si modules; SPRAT-27 talk has no proceedings.
